searches.reason: Develop a practical context-intervention probe for GRU4Rec: compare full histories, removed old prefixes, and removed recent suffixes while holding targets and candidate sets fixed. Measure paired rank changes by history length and elapsed time, with user-level bootstrap intervals. This can distinguish harmful historical carryover from useful long-term context and motivate stochastic prefix removal without changing supervision.

searches.reason: Translate qualitative feedback into evidence-backed diagnostics for the twenty training users receiving full-catalog recommendations. Research structured annotation that separates immediate choice, deferred interest, duplication, compatibility concerns, and unidentified content. Use only available titles, descriptions, timestamps, histories, and actual feedback; assess annotation agreement and abstain when evidence is insufficient. This could expose why broadly related recommendations fail without inventing ownership facts or latent user traits.
searches.query: recommendation evaluation intent grounded user feedback annotation immediate choice deferred interest functional redundancy compatibility uncertainty abstention 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Establish whether diagnostic improvements predict useful ranking changes. Examine repeated diagnostic candidate samples, training-popularity and history-length strata, and paired uncertainty estimates to test whether positive–negative margins or context sensitivity track the fixed host validation HR@10 across all four datasets. Keep diagnostic rankings distinct from benchmark scores and use full-catalog diagnostics only on training histories. This should reveal misleading easy-negative gains and identify reliable signals for revising one GRU4Rec model per category.
